gap: No result ChatGPT got states that ChatGPT's two HDMI picks differ on the feature that decides whether one monitor works smoothly between two computers. The $129.99 TESmart HKS201-P23 has EDID emulation, which stops windows rearranging on a switch, and keyboard-hotkey switching. The single-monitor UGREEN HDMI KVM it ranked first has neither, so each time you switch, the computer you left can act as if its monitor was unplugged.
standout_why: I read the two cited rivals. iTechGuides already says 'EDID emulation is not supported' and 'Not support Keyboard shortcuts (hotkeys) toggles' about a UGREEN listing, but for the 2-monitor model. It also explains that the computer you switch away from 'may believe the display has been unplugged'. DeskDNA says EDID emulation 'stops your windows rearranging every time you switch machines', but credits it only to the TESmart DisplayPort 1.4 KVM ($160) and calls it 'rare on cheap ones'. Neither page applies this to ChatGPT's actual single-monitor UGREEN pick, and neither says the TESmart HKS201-P23 ($129.99, HDMI) has it. So the mechanism is already known, and the new part is only which of ChatGPT's two products has it. I could not read thisUSB (certificate error) or the uncited results.
decides: This changes the pick for anyone who leaves windows open on both computers. ChatGPT's 'best overall value' UGREEN lacks EDID emulation and hotkeys and does not work with docking stations, so every switch can rearrange windows on the computer you left, and you switch with a button or desk controller. TESmart HKS201-P23 has the same 4K60 HDMI 2.0 video and, per its maker, both features, for $129.99. Both HDMI picks top out at 2560×1440 @ 120 Hz, so the owner of a 1440p 144/165 Hz monitor needs a DisplayPort 1.4 KVM. StarTech's DP 1.4 model says 'DSC support required for maximum performance', so the graphics card and monitor must both support DSC (Display Stream Compression) to get 4K 144 Hz.

findings.label: Why EDID emulation matters
findings.value: Without it, 'the inactive computer may behave as if the monitor was unplugged'; 'those windows may all move to one screen or shift to unexpected positions'; a monitor 'may fall back to a lower refresh rate'
findings.source_title: EDID Emulation Explained: How It Makes KVM Multi-Monitor Switching More Stable – TESmart (May 14, 2026)
findings.note: Maker's explanation. With emulation, the computer you switched away from keeps 'receiving consistent display identity information from the KVM', which 'helps the operating system keep the display recognized as connected'. TESmart sells KVMs, so this is a vendor source.
